description: Capytaine is a Python package for frequency-domain interaction between water waves and floating bodies, maintained by Matthieu Ancellin and the Capytaine developers. It rewrites the Nemoh boundary-element solver around linear potential-flow theory. The documented quickstart loads a body mesh, defines degrees of freedom, wave frequencies, directions and water depth, and exports calculated results to NetCDF. Coverage is global at body scale, with mesh and frequency resolution selected by the user, not an observed time series. Packages for Windows, macOS and Linux and public documentation are free under Apache-2.0 from version 3. A limitation is the linear potential-flow formulation: its stated scope should not be confused with a general nonlinear viscous-flow solver. Older releases have different licence history, and the standalone executable has documented drawbacks. The package can prepare hydrodynamic inputs for offshore-energy or floating-structure studies, complementary to the wind-turbine digital twin (model-wtdigitwin-wind-turbine-digital-twin). The JOSS article describes the software. No mesh, model archive or simulation output was downloaded.
